thread.title: Record number of Arizona students earn Seal of Arts Proficiency
thread.title_full: Record number of Arizona students earn Seal of Arts Proficiency

author: Grand Canyon Times
title: Record number of Arizona students earn Seal of Arts Proficiency
text:
Tom Horne Superintendent | Arizona Department of Education
Tom Horne Superintendent | Arizona Department of Education
Nearly 2,400 students in Arizona public schools received the Seal of Arts Proficiency during the 2024-25 school year, marking a record high. The Dysart Unified School District led with 249 recipients.
State schools superintendent Tom Horne expressed satisfaction with the achievement. "I am a passionate supporter of the arts," he said. "Not only do disciplines such as music, theatre, art and dance have intrinsic value, but studies have proven that students who pursue the arts often do better academically. There is tremendous value in arts education, and I am extremely pleased to see the highest number of students in the history of this program receiving the Seal of Arts Proficiency. I also offer my congratulations to the Dysart district and its leadership for having the most students receiving this recognition."
The program, initiated in 2019, aims to celebrate students' proficiency in arts standards, identify pathways for artistic literacy that cultivate life skills, prepare students for college and career readiness, and promote access to arts education across Arizona.
The state's arts and culture sector accounts for nearly 80,000 jobs. The Seal of Proficiency helps prepare students with skills necessary for success in creative industries and personal growth. A total of 2,366 Seals were awarded this year, with some students earning more than one.
